stem.text: Find the particular solution to the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} = \cos{\left(x^{2} \right)} \) with the initial condition \( y(0) = - \frac{1}{2} \), written in terms of a definite integral.

worked_solution.text: The right side depends on x alone and has no elementary antiderivative, so accumulate it from the initial input: \( \int_{0}^{x} \cos{\left(t^{2} \right)}\,dt \) is the change in y from x = 0.
Add the initial value: \( y = - \frac{1}{2} + \int_{0}^{x} \cos{\left(t^{2} \right)}\,dt \), which equals \( - \frac{1}{2} \) at x = 0 and has derivative \( \cos{\left(x^{2} \right)} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: initial value plus the accumulated change

options.label: \( y = \cos{\left(x^{2} \right)} - \frac{3}{2} \)
options.derivation: the given rate treated as though it were the quantity itself, shifted to pass through the initial point

options.label: \( y = - \frac{1}{2} + \int_{0}^{x} \cos{\left(t^{2} \right)} \)
options.derivation: the initial value and the integral written with the differential dt left off

options.label: \( y = \int_{0}^{x} \cos{\left(t^{2} \right)}\,dt \)
options.derivation: the accumulated change written alone, without the initial value
